title: Arne Slot says he expects Liverpool’s Wataru Endo to be out ‘for quite a long time’
content:
Liverpool head coach Arne Slot says Wataru Endo’s injury “doesn’t look good” and expects the midfielder to have a sustained spell on the sidelines.

Endo was stretchered off the pitch at the Stadium of Light in Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Sunderland on Wednesday. The 33-year-old started at right-back in the game and appeared to land awkwardly on his ankle after blocking a shot in the second half. He attempted to continue playing but went down after the ball went out of play and was treated for several minutes before being carried off the field and replaced by Joe Gomez.

“His injury doesn’t look good,” Slot told TNT Sports after the game. “I expect him to be out unfortunately for quite a long time again. What a mentality for him as well that things really didn’t look good but he stayed on the pitch and defended one more set piece.”

Speaking shortly afterwards during his post-match press conference, Slot said: “It’s a serious one. How serious we don’t know yet. He has to be assessed tomorrow.

“Foot (injury), we don’t know what it is yet, but it will be assessed tomorrow.

“I assume he will be out for a long time. You can hardly believe what has happened in this right-back position.”

Endo has appeared 12 times for Liverpool this campaign and missed a month with an ankle issue picked up in December.

The injury comes at a tough time for Liverpool, who have been heavily affected by injuries at the back. Endo started at right-back in the absence of Jeremie Frimpong, who has been out since late January with a groin issue, and Conor Bradley, who underwent surgery for a season-ending knee injury last month.

Midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai has featured at right-back this season, though he missed the Sunderland game through suspension after receiving a straight red card in Liverpool’s 2-1 defeat against Manchester City on Sunday.

Gomez, who is capable of playing across the back four, is a candidate to play at right-back. Midfielder Curtis Jones has been deployed in the position, while Calvin Ramsay could also step in, though he has only appeared once for Liverpool this term.

Liverpool are next in action on Saturday when they host Brighton & Hove Albion in the FA Cup fourth round.
